sections.markdown:
## C2 — Sharing-the-road confusables with knowledge-graph hints

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A96
On a two-lane road, oncoming drivers stop for a school bus with flashing red lights just like drivers behind it, and they move on only after the lights stop, the sign retracts and the arm returns to the bumper. [A96]
Why it matters: group_hint school-bus; prereq_hint sec07-F06; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F10, sec07-F11.
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A97
The multilane exception helps only oncoming traffic; anyone traveling behind the bus on any multilane road must still stop. [A97]
Why it matters: group_hint school-bus; prereq_hint sec07-R01; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec07-F11.
Source: [A97 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A95
A center turn lane is not a way around a stopped school bus, because drivers in every turn lane must stop too. [A95]
Why it matters: group_hint school-bus; prereq_hint sec07-F07; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F08.
Source: [A95 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A93
A pedestrian without a mobility aid must clear your lane and one more before you go, but a pedestrian with a wheelchair, cane or service animal must reach the far side of the street. [A93]
Why it matters: group_hint pedestrians; prereq_hint sec07-F02; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec07-F03.
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A105
The railroad stop zone is no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, and flashing lights with bells mean stop even when the gate is still up. [A105]
Why it matters: group_hint railroad; prereq_hint sec07-F29; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec07-F30, sec07-F31.
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A106
A problem on the tracks goes first to the number on the blue and white Emergency Notification System sign, and 911 is the fallback only when no sign is posted. [A106]
Why it matters: group_hint railroad; prereq_hint sec07-F32; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F33.
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A103
The 3-foot passing gap for a bicyclist is measured from the widest part of your vehicle, and with one lane each way you use the other lane only when no traffic is coming. [A103]
Why it matters: group_hint bicyclists; prereq_hint sec07-F24; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec07-F25, sec07-F27.
Source: [A103 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A103
A bicyclist on the road is treated as a vehicle with a right to the full lane, but a bicyclist in a crosswalk is treated as a pedestrian you must yield to. [A103]
Why it matters: group_hint bicyclists; prereq_hint sec07-F24; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F26.
Source: [A103 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A99
Before merging ahead of a large vehicle you need both of its headlights in your rearview mirror, not just one, and after merging you keep pace with traffic rather than slowing in front of it. [A99]
Why it matters: group_hint large-vehicles; prereq_hint sec07-F13; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F15.
Source: [A99 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A102
A motorcycle can slow down with no brake light showing, and its turn signal may still blink after the turn, so neither light alone tells you what the rider will do. [A102]
Why it matters: group_hint motorcycles; prereq_hint sec07-F19; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F23.
Source: [A102 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A107
For an emergency vehicle you pull to the right and stop as soon as you see or hear it, and you signal and rejoin traffic in your original order only once it has gone by. [A107]
Why it matters: group_hint emergency-vehicles; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec07-F36.
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0107]
